docs.text: Database indexes are data structures that speed up query execution. B-tree indexes support range scans while hash indexes excel at point lookups. Good index design reduces disk I/O dramatically.
Transactions guarantee ACID properties: atomicity, consistency, isolation and durability. Concurrent control is implemented through locking and multiversion concurrency control.
Query optimizers translate SQL into efficient execution plans using cost models. EXPLAIN helps developers analyze slow queries by showing index usage and join order.
Vector databases store high-dimensional embeddings and perform approximate nearest neighbor search. They power semantic search and retrieval augmented generation applications.
HNSW builds a hierarchical navigable small world graph for fast approximate search. It navigates coarse layers first, then refines, visiting only a few nodes per query.
Hybrid search combines vector semantic search with keyword full-text search. Reciprocal rank fusion merges the two ranked lists into one final ordering.
Embedding models like Sentence-BERT and BGE encode text into dense vectors. all-MiniLM-L6-v2 is a compact English model that runs well on edge devices.
Vector index quantization such as product quantization compresses vectors to save memory. It trades a little accuracy for much higher throughput on large datasets.
Inverted indexes map each term to the documents that contain it, enabling fast keyword lookup. BM25 scores documents by term frequency, inverse document frequency and length normalization.
MySQL full-text search uses MATCH AGAINST with natural language or boolean modes. Boolean mode supports AND, OR and NOT operators for complex queries.
Search engines separate retrieval into recall and ranking stages. Recall gathers candidates from the inverted index while ranking re-scores them with heavier models.
Stop words like the, a, and of are filtered during indexing because they carry little retrieval value. Stemming reduces words to their roots to compress the index.
Machine learning learns patterns from data. Supervised learning needs labeled examples for classification and regression, while unsupervised learning discovers structure without labels.
Overfitting happens when a model memorizes training data but fails on new data. Regularization, dropout, data augmentation and early stopping improve generalization.
Gradient descent optimizes model parameters by stepping against the loss gradient. Minibatch gradient descent balances stability and speed between batch and stochastic variants.
Precision, recall and F1 are standard metrics for classification. They matter more than accuracy when classes are imbalanced.
Neural networks stack layers of neurons with weights and activation functions. Backpropagation computes parameter gradients and updates weights layer by layer.
The Transformer architecture relies on self-attention and processes sequences in parallel. Multi-head attention captures relationships from different representation subspaces.
Quantization converts floating point weights into low precision formats such as FP16 or INT8. Quantized models are smaller and faster, making them ideal for on-device inference.
Attention mechanisms let a model focus on the most relevant parts of the input when generating each output token.
WebAssembly is a low-level bytecode that runs in browsers at near-native speed. Combined with onnxruntime-web it enables neural network inference inside the browser.
WebGPU is the modern browser API for GPU computing. It gives web pages direct access to the graphics processor for high performance parallel workloads.
Service Workers intercept network requests and manage caches for offline apps. Combined with the Cache API they enable offline-first web applications.
On-device AI runs models directly on user hardware instead of uploading data to the cloud. It protects privacy, reduces latency, and works offline at the cost of local compute.
